format_note: Descriptive contract, not a JSON Schema. xtask's enzyme-evidence-graph-check command now enforces a fail-closed structural/provenance subset; see ENZYME_EVIDENCE_GRAPH_VERIFIER_V0.md. Full replay, scientific semantics, and policy enforcement remain future work.
purpose: Bind each enzyme kinetic claim to exact source artifacts and the transformations, models, parameters, uncertainty, and evaluation decisions derived from them. Reuse EnzymeML/SBML for scientific objects; this contract addresses provenance and replay links.
design_principles: A reported literature value, a raw measurement, a reproduced fit, and a prediction are distinct evidence classes.
Every derived result must name its exact input node IDs, transformation, code/version, configuration and output artifacts.
A content hash proves byte identity, not license clearance, experimental validity, or scientific truth.
Missing or failed evidence is explicit; it is never represented as numeric zero or silently removed.
The graph is immutable per run; revisions create a new graph version with parent links rather than rewriting past receipts.

field_rules.artifact_id: Unique stable identifier within the graph.
field_rules.role: One of source_record, raw_signal, control_signal, calibration, processed_measurement, model_specification, fit_output, reported_parameter_table, prediction_output, evaluation_output, supporting_metadata, transformation_code, transformation_configuration, or environment_lock.
field_rules.media_type: Declared media type; not inferred from filename alone.
field_rules.sha256: 64 hexadecimal characters computed over the exact bytes consumed or produced.
field_rules.byte_length: Non-negative integer matching the exact payload length.
field_rules.locator: HTTPS URL or approved workspace-relative path. A remote URL must be acquired and hash-verified before the artifact may satisfy a replay requirement.
field_rules.rights_record_id: Reference to a separate source-specific rights/attribution review record. A checksum is not a rights grant.
field_rules.acquisition_status: available means an exact local workspace-relative payload is checked for byte length and SHA-256; not_acquired means HTTPS metadata only and is never downloaded by the verifier.

node_types.description: Versioned dataset/publication/record locator with source-specific rights receipt.
Raw instrument signal or measured time course with units, times, controls and instrument provenance where available.
Blank, no-enzyme, background, or other control observations with their own identities.
Calibration series, declared fit range, method/equation, coefficients, statistics and exact source/output artifacts.
Measurement after explicitly declared calibration, background correction, unit transformation or preprocessing.
Initial rate or time-course-derived rates, window and estimation method, uncertainty and exclusions.
Kinetic equation, variables, parameter meanings, constraints, initial conditions and applicable context.
One execution of a specified model and fitting algorithm with configuration, environment, outputs, logs and terminal status.
Parameter value exactly as reported by a source, retaining original units, context, uncertainty and source locator.
Parameter estimate independently recomputed from source measurement artifacts and a declared model/fit procedure.
A model output for a declared target, input context, model revision and uncertainty/abstention status.
Frozen held-out evaluation result, scorer revision, denominator, metrics, uncertainty and negative-control outcomes.

edge_types.description: States the source lineage for an artifact or scientific claim.
Optional relation grouping a measurement series with an associated control; explicit control IDs remain separate nodes.
Records which calibration was used in a transformation.
Records a control series used in a correction.
Explicit transformation dependency; exact dependency set must also appear in a transformation record.
Binds equation and parameterization to a specific fit execution.
Links one execution to parameters it estimates.
Links a reported value to its exact record/table/figure/page locator.
Binds a prediction to a model revision and target/context.
Links predictions to a frozen, independent scorer and evaluation split.

rules: Every referenced node and artifact ID must resolve exactly once.
Every input and output artifact must be hash/length verified against its recorded bytes.
Code/configuration/environment identities are distinct from the data artifact hashes.
A successful status requires every declared output to exist and match its hash.
A failed/blocked/excluded transformation remains in the graph with a reason; it is not omitted.
A replay result compares stage outputs and declared tolerances, not only the final kcat value.

conditional_artifact_fields.code_artifact_id: When present, references an artifact with role transformation_code whose exact-byte SHA-256 equals code_sha256. Required and byte-verified for successful transformations.
conditional_artifact_fields.configuration_artifact_id: When present, references an artifact with role transformation_configuration whose exact-byte SHA-256 equals configuration_sha256. Required and byte-verified for successful transformations.
conditional_artifact_fields.environment_lock_artifact_id: When present, references an artifact with role environment_lock whose exact-byte SHA-256 equals environment_lock_sha256. Required and byte-verified for successful transformations.
conditional_artifact_fields.note: These identity artifacts are separate from scientific input/output artifacts. Unsuccessful/blocked transformations may omit them if execution never started.

rules: A reported source parameter retains the verbatim source value/unit and a separate normalized value/unit when conversion is reviewed.
A fitted value is not relabeled as a directly measured datum.
kcat is not merged with Km, kcat/Km, Vmax, specific activity, yield, or activity without an explicitly defined conversion/model.
The subunit/oligomer concentration basis is explicit; if uncertain, comparability is blocked or qualified.

When source_or_fit_node_id identifies a source_record, a reported_by edge to a reported_parameter_claim node is required; when it identifies a fit_run, an estimates edge to a reproduced_parameter_estimate node is required.
Missing uncertainty is not encoded as zero uncertainty.

graph_invariants: Unknown fields in typed graph records are rejected rather than silently ignored.
Every declared artifact is referenced by an evidence node or transformation input/output/execution-identity field.
Every node ID and artifact ID is unique within a graph version.
Every edge endpoint resolves to a declared node; dangling edges fail closed.
Derivation edges form a directed acyclic graph; provenance references may point to shared upstream source nodes.
Every derived/fitted/predicted node has at least one explicit derivation/model edge and a matching transformation record, except source records and directly observed inputs.
Predictions, source-reported claims, and independently reproduced estimates use distinct node types and evidence classes.
Every terminal run status and exclusion/failure reason remains represented; no denominator is silently reduced.
Raw artifact hashes are verified against exact payload bytes before the corresponding artifact is marked acquired or replayable.
The evidence graph's own serialized bytes are versioned and SHA-256 pinned when frozen.
future_verifier_checks: Verify the execution semantics of the pinned source/configuration/environment artifacts and reproduce stage outputs in an independently implemented replay runner; matching identity hashes alone do not prove the declared code performed the claimed transform.
Finalize and enforce a JSON Schema for the instance layout.
Semantic-unit checks and parameter meaning using the selected EnzymeML version rather than a duplicate ontology.
Chemical reaction-balance checks where appropriate; this must be a separate domain-aware validator.
Human review and evidence for source-specific rights/attribution decisions; software status labels do not establish legal clearance.
A separately implemented computational replay verifier that compares every required pipeline-stage output within preregistered tolerances.
Independent checks of uncertainty calibration, parameter identifiability, model ambiguity, denominator accounting, and negative controls.
Prospective experimental-decision utility and generalization under study, sequence-family, laboratory/protocol, and assay-context holdouts.

Validate exact parameter source-value provenance and conversion-rule identity for normalized values; V0 checks the presence/type pairing of normalized value and unit but does not re-perform unit conversion.
non_claims: The Rust verifier implements only a structural/provenance subset. Scientific semantics, legal clearance, and actual computational replay remain unimplemented.
It does not establish that source data are scientifically valid or that a reaction equation is chemically balanced.
It does not automatically clear source licenses or sequence-data benefit-sharing obligations.
It does not implement a kinetic solver, protein predictor, prospective experiment system, or laboratory automation.

references.name: Reproducibility of enzyme reactions and kinetic modelling

graph_instance_v0.note: The record layout is a V0 implementation convention documented in ENZYME_EVIDENCE_GRAPH_VERIFIER_V0.md, not a finalized JSON Schema. Rust unit tests compare the executable checker vocabularies against these machine-readable enumerations. Frozen graphs require an external SHA-256 pin of their exact serialized bytes.

v0_implemented_checks: Unique IDs for node, edge, artifact, rights-record, transformation, and parameter-claim records.
Contract node-type/evidence-class consistency; known edge types and endpoint type constraints.
Exact byte-length and SHA-256 verification for acquired local artifacts; workspace confinement and symlink-escape protection.
HTTPS-only metadata locators for not-acquired artifacts; no automatic remote fetch.
Transformation input/output node and artifact reference closure, explicit dependency edges, and verified artifacts for successful transformations.
Explicit terminal reason for non-success transformations; null_result cannot claim outputs.
Parameter-claim uncertainty-status vocabulary and source/fit-node reference checks.
External exact-byte SHA-256 pin requirement for frozen graph inputs.
Successful transformations may use and publish only artifacts whose linked rights record declares approved_for_this_use; this is enforcement of a recorded status, not legal adjudication.
Parameter claim source values must be a JSON number or non-empty verbatim string; optional normalized_value and normalized_unit must appear together, and normalized_value is numeric.
Parameter claims require at least one unique substrate ID; missing substrate identity must be represented explicitly rather than as an empty list.

For successful transformations, code/configuration/environment-lock fingerprints resolve to separate artifacts with matching declared SHA-256, verified local bytes, and approved-for-this-use rights status.

The Rust unit suite loads this contract and compares node/evidence-class, edge, artifact-role, graph-status, rights-status, acquisition-status, terminal-status, and uncertainty vocabularies against executable policy constants.
